decisions.quote:
Although burrowing is a relatively novel pain outcome measure, a few studies have reported decreased burrowing in rat models of inflammatory and neuropathic pain; importantly, burrowing deficits were reversed by known analgesics, suggesting a degree of predictive validity for this outcome measure.2,9,20,35,61,62
We hypothesise that by using a prospective multicentre design, the reliability of novel outcome measures can be efficiently and rapidly evaluated. As part of the IMI Europain collaboration (http://www.imieuropain.org), we investigated rat burrowing behaviour after induction of complete Freund adjuvant (CFA)-associated inflammation across 8 centres to assess the reliability of suppressed burrowing as a pain-related outcome measure.
decisions.reason: Prior adjudication and state files are absent. This IMI Europain multicentre validation study retests CFA-induced suppression of rat burrowing originally reported by Andrews et al. (2012) [2] (already represented by shipped row 182, 10.1016/j.ejpain.2011.07.012), from which the experimental protocol was taken ('Burrowing experiments were performed as previously described.2,62', where [62] is Rutten et al. 2014 in a knee-joint inflammation model). Gould et al. (2016) [20] ('Pharmacological characterization of intraplantar Complete Freund's Adjuvant-induced burrowing deficits', Behav Brain Res 2016;301:142–51) was published in 2016—after all 11 multicentre experiments in the present study were completed between June 2013 and September 2014 (Results 3.1)—by co-author A. Pekcec's Boehringer Ingelheim group, and is cited only in a six-reference background cluster [2,9,20,35,61,62] and Discussion remarks [2,20,62] on analgesic reversal (ibuprofen vs. gabapentin), which this non-pharmacological study did not test.
